correctness.rationale: The theorem reduces to exactly 16384 possible closed-neighborhood code masks and 268 verified optimal size-seven masks. The characterizing signatures b_v AND c are necessary and sufficient for identification. For each unordered pair of optimal codes, exactly one token change is equivalent to XOR Hamming weight 2, and the additional incidence-edge test is necessary and sufficient for a slide. Two differently constructed full enumerators reproduced all 268 state masks and every one of the 210 slide edges (states.txt and slides.txt), independently computed 56 K1,3 and 2 K1,21 components, and checked their reachability. Component degree sequences force the star graph isomorphisms. The exact reachable distance histogram is 210 at distance 1 and 588 at distance 2; no infinite inference is made. Certificates regenerate from the embedded public code, not unverified logs.

The prior same-object code census and unrestricted token-JUMP classification is acknowledged as covered; it says nothing about which exchanges correspond to incidence edges, so it does not imply the slide-star decomposition from an abstract unmarked exchange-graph isomorphism. The directly inspected published identifying-code graph and reconfiguration sources do not give this fixed-input slide graph. The value and novelty attach only to the genuinely new restricted-move classification, not to the known 268-code count or jump-component geometry.

value.rationale: Adjacency-restricted slide mobility is the canonical identifying-code gamma-graph move model in Mynhardt--Teshima. For the classical smallest nontrivial projective-plane incidence graph, the complete 268-state slide graph fragments into 58 components but has no isolated minimum code, a sharp qualitative contrast to its already-known unrestricted 3-component jump geometry. Its exact 56 claws, two large stars, degree spectrum, and reachability distance histogram answer a natural complete fixed-object classification, not a chosen arbitrary parameter slice. In particular no slide sequence can escape its at-most-22-state star despite extensive jump mobility. This is meaningful structural information beyond the pre-existing code count and unmarked jump graph; no downstream theorem is asserted.
